data.title: Just Another Defeat on Facebook: "Nigel Spackman was preparing for the biggest match of his Rangers career when Walter S
data.content:
Tom Cowan broke his leg. John Brown was struggling with a calf problem. Players were forced to switch positions, with Spackman moving from midfield into central defence as Rangers reorganised.

Aberdeen were far from overwhelmed. Chris Woods made an important early save, and there was little to suggest Rangers were going to have an easy afternoon. [...] Smith's conversation concerned Ally McCoist and Ian Durrant. Both were injured, but the manager intended to name them among the substitutes.

His reasoning fascinated Spackman. If Rangers were behind or drawing, bringing either player on could lift the crowd and give the team the encouragement they needed.

It was an early glimpse of the thinking that would make Smith one of the most successful managers in Scottish football history. [...] The visitors also had their own selection problems. First-choice goalkeeper Theo Snelders was unavailable, leaving 20-year-old Michael Watt to face a Rangers attack led by Mark Hateley.

Hateley scored twice, heading Rangers in front before adding a second after the interval.

Rangers won 2-0.

For Spackman, the afternoon ended with an honour he could scarcely have anticipated when he arrived from QPR in November 1989.
